summary: Behind [asks] deadlines, off by default: every person ask has a deadline (24h unless the ask or `[asks] default_deadline` says otherwise) and an optional default answer; an unanswered ask resolves by itself at its deadline, recorded as resolved by deadline, and the asking step resumes

replay.detail: No graph replay. An ask made by an older build, or while deadlines were off, has no deadline field; its deadline is counted from the first reconcile pass that saw [asks] deadlines on (person_ask_deadlines_since_unix_ms, written once into meta), so open asks do not all resolve when deadlines are turned on.

schema.detail: Additive claim fields: work.person-asked gains deadline_unix_ms, deadline_ms (only when the asker named a deadline) and default_answer, work.person-done and work.person-cancelled gain resolved_by. One meta key, local to the member, written when deadlines are first on. While [asks] deadlines is off none of the new fields is written. Storage version is unchanged.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: A member on an older build does not know the new claim fields and keeps such claims as retryable until it upgrades, so [asks] deadlines is off by default and nothing writes them until it is turned on. The client contract gains work.ask deadline_ms and default_answer, an optional resolved_by field on answers, and a respondent that may be daemon/runtime (RespondentRef; it already is for an ask its requester's end cancelled). No answer outcome is added: an ask resolved at its deadline carries its default answer with that answer's own outcome (accept, decline or selected), or no answer. An older TypeScript client ignores resolved_by and reads the answer, but refuses daemon/runtime as a respondent, which the schema test records; Rust and Swift read it as a string. While deadlines are off, work.ask refuses deadline_ms and default_answer with ask-deadlines-off. Rollout: daemons and the web client first, then turn the option on. A person's answer made on another member before the deadline wins over a default the ask's own member applied, on every member, and its asker is told once. A new CLI against an older daemon does not know to refuse --deadline and --default: the older daemon ignores them and asks without a deadline.

downtime.detail: No downtime. The meta key is written by the first reconcile pass that sees [asks] deadlines on and has asks open, not at store open.

manual.detail: After every member and the web client run this build, an operator sets [asks] deadlines = true in each daemon config (it reloads with the other daemon policies, no restart). Optionally [asks] default_deadline (1m to 30d).

recovery.detail: Set [asks] deadlines = false to stop new deadlines and resolutions at once; the next pass forgets the count, so turning them on again counts open asks afresh. To revert to a build without this change, first delete the [asks] section from every daemon config: an older build refuses unknown config fields. An older build keeps claims carrying the new fields as retryable; asks already resolved by deadline stay resolved.
